terminal.description: A shell in your workspace, already pointed at the offline local model.

tasks.title: Compare two runs case by case
tasks.description:
In `src/compare.ts`, implement `compareRuns(baseline: RunResult, candidate: RunResult): Comparison`.

Return `{ baseline, candidate, baselineRate, candidateRate, fixed, broken, unchanged }`:

- `baseline` and `candidate`: the two model names
- the rates: passing cases divided by all cases for each run, or `0` for a run with no cases
- `fixed`: ids that failed on the baseline and pass on the candidate
- `broken`: ids that passed on the baseline and fail on the candidate
- `unchanged`: every other id

All three lists follow the baseline's case order. Match cases by id: the candidate run may list them in a different order. Both runs must cover the same ids; if an id is in one run but not the other, throw an `Error` that contains that id.
nextSteps: Index the candidate's outcomes by id.
Walk the baseline cases in order and sort each id into one of the three lists.
Check for ids that only one run has, in both directions.
hints: Two runs over the same set can still list cases in a different order, for example when requests finish at different times.
A `Map` from id to `passed` gives you the candidate outcome for any baseline id in one lookup. A missing entry means the runs do not match.
Checking baseline ids against the candidate map finds one direction. Also look for candidate ids that are not in the baseline before you start sorting.

tasks.title: Write the ship rule
tasks.description:
In `src/decide.ts`, implement:

- `decide(comparison: Comparison): Decision`, returning `{ ship, reasons }`. The team's rule: no case that passed on the baseline may break. Any broken id means `ship: false`, with one reason per broken id that contains the id. A comparison with no cases at all means `ship: false`, with a reason that contains `no cases`. Otherwise `ship: true` and `reasons: []`.
- `compareModels(cases, baselineModel, candidateModel)`: run both models with `runCases`, compare the runs with `compareRuns`, and return `{ comparison, decision }`.

A higher pass rate does not override the rule. The check runs `decide` on hand-made comparisons and `compareModels` on hidden cases with the real triage models.
nextSteps: Turn each broken id into a reason.
Write `compareModels` with the functions you already have.
hints: The decision depends on the lists, not on the two rates.
`broken.map(id => ...)` gives you the reasons; `ship` is whether that list is empty.
Both model runs are independent, so `Promise.all` can run them side by side.

tasks.title: Test the ship rule
tasks.description:
Write vitest tests in `src/decide.test.ts` that pin the ship rule down. They should check that:

- a candidate that breaks a case that passed before is not shipped, even when its pass rate is higher
- each broken id appears in the reasons
- a candidate with no broken cases is shipped
- a comparison with no cases is not shipped

The check runs your test file three times: beside an unfinished `decide.ts` (it must fail), beside a correct one (it must pass) and beside one that ships whenever the pass rate does not drop (it must fail). Build your comparisons by hand or with `compareRuns`; do not call the model.
nextSteps: Write a small helper that builds a `RunResult` from ids and pass flags.
Write one test per rule in the task.
Ask which of your tests a rate-only rule would still pass.
hints: Tests that only use cases where the rate and the rule agree cannot tell the two rules apart.
Make a candidate that fixes two cases and breaks one. Its rate goes up, and the rule must still say no.
`expect(decision.ship).toBe(false)` plus `expect(decision.reasons.join(' ')).toContain(id)` covers the first two rules for that case.
